choices: Approve — 20 consecutive green CI runs are strong evidence the race is gone
Approve, but change `VLOG` to `LOG(INFO)` so it also works in release builds
Reject: it's a timing-based fake fix; synchronize on the real condition
Ask for a `std::this_thread::yield()` too, so the other thread reliably gets scheduled
explain: Logging, dummy work, reordering, and yields only change timing; they hide the race instead of fixing it. Never use a timing-based fix; add proper synchronization.

prompt: A test sometimes checks `tab_helper()->PageDistillState()` before distillation finishes. Which fix addresses the root cause?
choices: `ASSERT_TRUE(base::test::RunUntil([&] { return tab_helper()->PageDistillState() == kDistilled; }));`
`base::PlatformThread::Sleep(base::Milliseconds(500));` before checking `PageDistillState()`
`base::RunLoop().RunUntilIdle();` then `ASSERT_EQ(tab_helper()->PageDistillState(), DistillState::kDistilled);`
`ASSERT_TRUE(content::NavigateToURL(web_contents, url));` again, then check `PageDistillState()`
explain: Proper root cause analysis means identifying what races and waiting on the actual condition you care about (`RunUntil`, `TestFuture`, observers), not on arbitrary time.

prompt: A teammate says: "I extracted a helper method and the flake went away. If I inline it again, it flakes. Not sure why, but it works." How should you respond?
choices: Ship it — the extracted helper is cleaner code, so the refactor is an improvement anyway
Ship it, with a comment saying not to inline the helper
It's not a fix: without explaining the synchronization, the race is still there
Run it 100 times locally under load; if it never fails, the race is effectively fixed
explain: If removing your "fix" brings the flake back but you can't explain WHY it fixes the race, it's not a real fix. Real fixes are deterministic, explainable, and robust.

choices: Nothing — `RunUntilIdle()` drains every pending task, so the sync result is deterministic
It should call `RunUntilIdle()` twice, since sync may post a follow-up task
It should use `ASSERT_TRUE` so a failed sync stops the test immediately
`RunUntilIdle()` is forbidden: it can return early or time out; wait on the condition
explain: Chromium style forbids `RunLoop::RunUntilIdle()` for async tests. It can return too early when events depend on other task queues, or run too long, which makes tests flaky.

prompt: A browser test must wait until the Speedreader bubble appears, i.e. until `tab_helper()->speedreader_bubble_view()` is non-null. Which wait follows the standard?
choices: Loop `NonBlockingDelay(base::Milliseconds(100))` until `speedreader_bubble_view()` is non-null
`ASSERT_TRUE(base::test::RunUntil([this]() { return tab_helper()->speedreader_bubble_view(); }));`
`base::RunLoop().RunUntilIdle();` then `ASSERT_TRUE(tab_helper()->speedreader_bubble_view());`
`EXPECT_TRUE(content::EvalJs(web_contents, "!!document.querySelector('#speedreader-bubble')"))`
explain: To wait on C++ state or object properties, use `base::test::RunUntil()` with a lambda that checks the condition directly.

choices: `EvalJs` spins its own run loop; don't nest run-loop operations inside `RunUntil`
Nothing — `RunUntil` is designed for polling JS state, and `EvalJs` is synchronous
It should use `ExecJs`, because `EvalJs(...).ExtractBool()` crashes on non-bool values
The lambda should capture `web_contents` by value, since `RunUntil` may call it later
explain: Never call something that spins its own run loop (`EvalJs`, `ExecJs`, IPC that waits for a response) inside `RunUntil()`. Only direct C++ state checks, getters, and property checks are safe.

choices: Nothing — `RunLoop` plus `BindLambdaForTesting` is the canonical callback-waiting pattern
Replace `run_loop.Run()` with `RunUntilIdle()` so the test can't hang if the callback never fires
Use `run_loop.QuitClosure()` instead of calling `Quit()` in the lambda
Use `base::test::TestFuture<bool>`: pass `future.GetCallback()`, check `future.Get()`
explain: Always use `base::test::TestFuture` for `OnceCallback`-based operations; it's shorter and less error-prone. Reviewers flag `RunLoop` + `BindLambdaForTesting` + `Quit()` when `TestFuture` would work.

prompt: A browser test sends `Init()` asynchronously over the Solana provider Mojo interface, then needs to be sure it was processed before asserting. Which approach is precise and deterministic?
choices: `base::PlatformThread::Sleep(base::Milliseconds(100))`, which covers Mojo's typical latency
A sync call on the same interface, e.g. read `window.braveSolana.isConnected`
Call `RunUntilIdle()` in both the browser and renderer processes to flush the Mojo pipe
Send `Init()` twice so at least one is processed
explain: Mojo processes messages in order on a given interface. A synchronous call on that interface guarantees all earlier async messages on it have been handled, which is a precise alternative to polling.

prompt: `object_under_test.DoSomethingAsync(base::OnceClosure done)` takes a plain closure, and you need manual run-loop control that `TestFuture` doesn't give you. What's the accepted pattern?
choices: Pass `base::DoNothing()` as `done`, then call `RunUntilIdle()` to drain the async work
Poll with `RunUntil` and an `ExecJs` check that the page reflects the result
Create a `base::RunLoop`, pass `run_loop.QuitClosure()`, then `run_loop.Run()`
Sleep briefly with `PlatformThread::Sleep`, then check the result object's state
explain: When `TestFuture` doesn't fit, pass `run_loop.QuitClosure()` and call `run_loop.Run()`, which waits specifically for that closure to fire.

choices: Wrap the `EvalJs` check in `base::test::RunUntil` so it retries until the setting applies
Add `RunUntilIdle()` between the two lines so the Mojo message is flushed first
Repeat the `EvalJs` check up to three times to absorb the Mojo round-trip latency
Pass a `TestFuture` callback to `UpdateSettings`, wait on `future.Get()`, then `EvalJs`
explain: Don't call `EvalJs` right after an async Mojo operation; the message may not be processed yet. Synchronize on the Mojo response first, with a `TestFuture` or `RunUntil` on C++ state.
